summary: Blaine County, ID: BLM two-story lookout built 1963, last staffed 1998, demolished 2014; the site now has antenna installations and a drive-up road.

facts.design: BLM-designed two-story lookout house with a concrete base and frame cab
facts.status_note: Demolished in 2014; a 2020 climbing guide says the former lookout site has several antenna installations

access.note: Road from Bellevue (Pine Street, then Sharps Canyon Road) reaches the summit; 4WD recommended; land is a mix of BLM, state and private, so check the BLM Fairfield map

events.note: Two-story lookout house designed by the BLM, with a concrete base and frame cab
Mr. and Mrs. Louis Anderson were the known lookout staff from 1963 to 1974; one site also names Thora Anderson
July 1970 Idaho Statesman item quoted on a lookout site: the Andersons would again be at the station east of Bellevue
Demolished in 2014; one site dates the removal to September 2014
Climbing guide updated September 2020 describes several antenna installations at the former lookout site and a road to the top

notes_for_editor: The 1963 build, the Anderson staffing, the 1998 last-staffed year and the 2014 demolition agree across three amateur lookout sites. The present state rests on one climbing guide updated September 2020 (antennas, road, land mix); no recent photo or BLM record was read. A BLM NEPA register entry (DOI-BLM-ID-T030-2014-0012-CX) appeared in search results but was not read; it may cover the 2014 work. Access is drive-up per the guide and the Idaho Fire Lookouts header; check current BLM land status before any stronger access claim. Brief coordinates differ from the weebly page by about 0.0001 degree, which is negligible.
